title: A Closed-Loop and Data-Driven Decoding Algorithm for Optical Pulse Position Modulated Uplinks in Neural Implants
titleZh: 面向神经植入器件光学 PPM 上行链路的闭环数据驱动解码
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
summary: An adaptive, closed-loop algorithm for detecting and decoding optical pulse position modulation signals under low and varying signal-to-noise ratios.
summaryZh: 针对低信噪比及信噪比波动的情况，通过自适应闭环算法检测并解码光学脉冲位置调制（PPM）信号。

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: An adaptive, closed-loop algorithm for detecting and decoding optical pulse position modulation signals under low and varying signal-to-noise ratios.

Proportional-integral feedback and a periodic microsystem clock provide reference enhancement. The decoding method is evaluated on a channel model based on experimental data from a neural recording microsystem.
paragraphsZh: 这项工作关注低信噪比及信噪比波动条件下的光学 PPM 信号，利用自适应闭环算法完成脉冲检测与信号解码。
通过比例–积分（PI）反馈和微系统的周期时钟增强参考信号，并基于神经记录微系统的实验数据建立信道模型，对解码方法进行评估。

sections.heading: Timing-guided detection
paragraphs: A MOTE encodes each sample as the delay between a periodic reference pulse and an encoding pulse. Under weak optical coupling, a low detection threshold introduces false alarms, while a high threshold misses real pulses.

PPM timing provides a way to recognize both errors. Inter-pulse intervals should fall within a valid range set by the clock period and minimum pulse separation. Violations of this timing structure provide feedback for threshold adaptation, without requiring a known pulse shape.

images.alt: Noisy PPM pulses and a valid inter-pulse timing range, illustrating false alarms below the range and missed detections above it
images.caption: Pulse timing reveals threshold errors: short intervals indicate false alarms, while long intervals indicate missed detections.

sections.heading: Closed-loop decoding
paragraphs: The decoder estimates signal parameters and adapts its threshold in a feedback loop. Once the threshold converges, reference calibration stabilizes the clock sequence before the neural waveform is reconstructed.
bullets: Initialize the threshold from a log-compressed amplitude histogram using an entropy-based criterion.
Estimate pulse width, inter-pulse separation, pulse centers, and oscillator period from the thresholded samples.
Use PI feedback to balance missed and spurious detections, then reduce timing jitter near the low-error operating point. Quantization-aware updates limit threshold dithering.
Calibrate the periodic reference sequence using its dominant phase and clock period, compensate missing reference pulses, and decode each encoding pulse relative to the stabilized references.

images.alt: Horizontal decoding workflow showing raw PPM samples, statistical threshold initialization, parameter estimation, PI feedback, reference calibration, and decoded output
images.caption: From noisy optical pulses to a decoded waveform through threshold adaptation and reference calibration.

sections.heading: Detection and decoding results
paragraphs: Evaluation combines labeled synthetic signals with measured MOTE uplinks. The synthetic signals reproduce the measured pulse width, clock period, and noise statistics, allowing detection accuracy to be compared over a range of SNRs.

PI feedback improves recall and F1 score over Otsu's method and Otsu-based thresholding, with a further improvement from reference calibration. Solid curves show mean performance and shaded bands show the minimum-to-maximum range. The measured waveform comparison demonstrates end-to-end decoding at approximately 7 dB SNR.

images.alt: Recall and F1 score across SNR levels, measured neural waveform reconstruction, and a close-up comparison of detected optical pulses
images.caption: Detection accuracy across SNR levels, reconstructed neural waveforms, and pulse-level comparisons.

sections.heading: Bench validation and power budget
paragraphs: An arbitrary waveform generator applies a prerecorded neural signal to a MOTE on a PCB. A photodetector and oscilloscope capture the resulting optical PPM uplink, providing a hardware test of the complete decoding chain.

At comparable recall and F1 levels, the decoder operates at a pulse power level 2.1 dB lower than the conventional baselines. For the MOTE power budget evaluated in this work, that improvement translates to 38% lower pulse-generation power and a 24% reduction in total system power requirement.

images.alt: Microscope and optical receiver above a MOTE on a PCB, with an arbitrary waveform generator and oscilloscope used for uplink measurements
images.caption: Hardware test bench for replaying neural signals through the MOTE optical uplink.
